itens.porque: Holding a position — and holding is legitimate. What it does not do is move the item forward.

itens.t: "What if we moved it to the start?"
itens.porque: A proposal: it gives the group something to accept or refuse.

itens.t: "So you would keep it, but not where it is."
itens.porque: Restating what someone else said. The most useful move in a three-voice call: it proves you followed, and it lets the other person correct you cheaply.

itens.t: "You are right about the hours. Not about the text."
itens.porque: Agreeing with part of it. Splitting the point is what keeps the disagreement about the text alive.
Asking to be told. Short, and it prevents the whole call from being read wrong afterwards.

itens.t: "Let us take it as a proposal and move on."
itens.porque: Closing the item. It is the chair’s move — done by anyone else, it can read as cutting the discussion off.

callout.titulo: The move that turned the call
callout.texto: Rachel did not contradict Peter. She refused the summary they had just agreed on — I am not sure we agree it is too long — and only then argued. Refusing the summary is how you move a conversation without making it a fight.

fourwaysatur.titulo: Four ways a turn can start
abertura: Use this whenever you want to review what you did in class.

tabela: Asking for the turn
Can I check one thing? · Sorry to jump in…
Without it you wait for a pause that never comes.
Anchoring in what was said
I heard you say… · You mentioned…
Opening your own subject makes the group choose between two conversations.
Asking for precision
Just to be clear… · Is that decided, or a proposal?
You leave with an answer that was never given.
Handing it back
That was all I needed. · Sorry, you were saying?
The call stalls and someone has to restart it for you.

itens.t: Giving her own opinion on the coursebook
itens.porque: She does not do this. Hearing an opinion where there is none is what makes people answer the wrong thing.

itens.t: Opening the item and handing the turn to someone
itens.porque: That is what she is doing — and it is the moment where entering costs nothing, because the floor is open.

itens.t: Asking Peter to change his view
itens.porque: She asks him to explain it, which is a different request.

sec4.rationale: She names the item, names the person and gives the turn away. That is chairing, and it is the whole of what she does.

itens.ok: the hours the unit really gets
itens.porque: The hours the unit really gets. It is the number in the plan.
The hours the document promises. Written in the syllabus, and the reason the difference matters.
The unit number. It sounds like the third figure in the same series and it is not a quantity at all — which is exactly how a briefing picks up a fourth divergence that does not exist.

nota.titulo: Two numbers for the same thing
nota.texto: Eighteen hours, twenty on paper — one is what happens, the other is what a document says. Which is which is not in the words: it is in on paper.
